items.title: Video generation models as world simulators
items.summary: We explore large-scale training of generative models on video data. Specifically, we train text-conditional diffusion models jointly on videos and images of variable durations, resolutions and aspect ratios. We leverage a transformer architecture that operates on spacetime patches of video and image latent codes. Our largest model, Sora, is capable of generating a minute of high fidelity video. Our results suggest that scaling video generation models is a promising path towards building general purpose simulators of the physical world.

items.title: Learning to play Minecraft with Video PreTraining

Our model uses the native human interface of keypresses and mouse movements, making it quite general, and represents a step towards general computer-using agents.

This shows promise for using AI systems to assist human supervision of AI systems on difficult tasks.

items.title: Language models are few-shot learners
AI and efficiency
items.summary: We’re releasing an analysis showing that since 2012 the amount of compute needed to train a neural net to the same performance on ImageNet classification has been decreasing by a factor of 2 every 16 months. Compared to 2012, it now takes 44 times less compute to train a neural network to the level of AlexNet (by contrast, Moore’s Law would yield an 11x cost improvement over this period). Our results suggest that for AI tasks with high levels of recent investment, algorithmic progress has yielded more gains than classical hardware efficiency.

items.title: Jukebox
items.summary: We’re introducing Jukebox, a neural net that generates music, including rudimentary singing, as raw audio in a variety of genres and artist styles. We’re releasing the model weights and code, along with a tool to explore the generated samples.

items.title: Improving verifiability in AI development
items.summary: We’ve contributed to a multi-stakeholder report by 58 co-authors at 30 organizations, including the Centre for the Future of Intelligence, Mila, Schwartz Reisman Institute for Technology and Society, Center for Advanced Study in the Behavioral Sciences, and Center for Security and Emerging Technologies. This report describes 10 mechanisms to improve the verifiability of claims made about AI systems. Developers can use these tools to provide evidence that AI systems are safe, secure, fair, or privacy-preserving. Users, policymakers, and civil society can use these tools to evaluate AI development processes.

items.title: OpenAI Microscope
items.summary: We’re introducing OpenAI Microscope, a collection of visualizations of every significant layer and neuron of eight vision “model organisms” which are often studied in interpretability. Microscope makes it easier to analyze the features that form inside these neural networks, and we hope it will help the research community as we move towards understanding these complicated systems.

items.title: OpenAI standardizes on PyTorch
items.summary: We are standardizing OpenAI’s deep learning framework on PyTorch.

items.title: Scaling laws for neural language models
Dota 2 with large scale deep reinforcement learning
Deep double descent
items.summary: We show that the double descent phenomenon occurs in CNNs, ResNets, and transformers: performance first improves, then gets worse, and then improves again with increasing model size, data size, or training time. This effect is often avoided through careful regularization. While this behavior appears to be fairly universal, we don’t yet fully understand why it happens, and view further study of this phenomenon as an important research direction.

items.title: Procgen Benchmark
items.summary: We’re releasing Procgen Benchmark, 16 simple-to-use procedurally-generated environments which provide a direct measure of how quickly a reinforcement learning agent learns generalizable skills.

items.title: Benchmarking safe exploration in deep reinforcement learning
Safety Gym
items.summary: We’re releasing Safety Gym, a suite of environments and tools for measuring progress towards reinforcement learning agents that respect safety constraints while training.

items.title: GPT-2: 1.5B release
items.summary: As the final model release of GPT-2’s staged release, we’re releasing the largest version (1.5B parameters) of GPT-2 along with code and model weights to facilitate detection of outputs of GPT-2 models. While there have been larger language models released since August, we’ve continued with our original staged release plan in order to provide the community with a test case of a full staged release process. We hope that this test case will be useful to developers of future powerful models, and we’re actively continuing the conversation with the AI community on responsible publication.

items.title: Solving Rubik’s Cube with a robot hand
items.summary: We’ve trained a pair of neural networks to solve the Rubik’s Cube with a human-like robot hand. The neural networks are trained entirely in simulation, using the same reinforcement learning code as OpenAI Five paired with a new technique called Automatic Domain Randomization (ADR). The system can handle situations it never saw during training, such as being prodded by a stuffed giraffe. This shows that reinforcement learning isn’t just a tool for virtual tasks, but can solve physical-world problems requiring unprecedented dexterity.

items.title: OpenAI Scholars 2020: Applications open
items.summary: We are now accepting applications for our third class of OpenAI Scholars.

items.title: Fine-tuning GPT-2 from human preferences
items.summary: We’ve fine-tuned the 774M parameter GPT-2 language model using human feedback for various tasks, successfully matching the preferences of the external human labelers, though those preferences did not always match our own. Specifically, for summarization tasks the labelers preferred sentences copied wholesale from the input (we’d only asked them to ensure accuracy), so our models learned to copy. Summarization required 60k human labels; simpler tasks which continue text in various styles required only 5k. Our motivation is to move safety techniques closer to the general task of “machines talking to humans,” which we believe is key to extracting information about human values.

items.title: Emergent tool use from multi-agent interaction
items.summary: We’ve observed agents discovering progressively more complex tool use while playing a simple game of hide-and-seek. Through training in our new simulated hide-and-seek environment, agents build a series of six distinct strategies and counterstrategies, some of which we did not know our environment supported. The self-supervised emergent complexity in this simple environment further suggests that multi-agent co-adaptation may one day produce extremely complex and intelligent behavior.

items.title: Testing robustness against unforeseen adversaries
items.summary: We’ve developed a method to assess whether a neural network classifier can reliably defend against adversarial attacks not seen during training. Our method yields a new metric, UAR (Unforeseen Attack Robustness), which evaluates the robustness of a single model against an unanticipated attack, and highlights the need to measure performance across a more diverse range of unforeseen attacks.

items.title: GPT-2: 6-month follow-up
items.summary: We’re releasing the 774 million parameter GPT-2 language model after the release of our small 124M model in February, staged release of our medium 355M model in May, and subsequent research with partners and the AI community into the model’s potential for misuse and societal benefit. We’re also releasing an open-source legal agreement to make it easier for organizations to initiate model-sharing partnerships with each other, and are publishing a technical report about our experience in coordinating with the wider AI research community on publication norms.

items.title: Learning Day
items.summary: At OpenAI, each Thursday is Learning Day: a day where employees have the option to self-study technical skills that will make them better at their job but which aren’t being learned from daily work.

items.title: Microsoft invests in and partners with OpenAI to support us building beneficial AGI
items.summary: Microsoft is investing $1 billion in OpenAI to support us building artificial general intelligence (AGI) with widely distributed economic benefits. We’re partnering to develop a hardware and software platform within Microsoft Azure which will scale to AGI. We’ll jointly develop new Azure AI supercomputing technologies, and Microsoft will become our exclusive cloud provider—so we’ll be working hard together to further extend Microsoft Azure’s capabilities in large-scale AI systems.

items.title: Why responsible AI development needs cooperation on safety
items.summary: We’ve written a policy research paper identifying four strategies that can be used today to improve the likelihood of long-term industry cooperation on safety norms in AI: communicating risks and benefits, technical collaboration, increased transparency, and incentivizing standards. Our analysis shows that industry cooperation on safety will be instrumental in ensuring that AI systems are safe and beneficial, but competitive pressures could lead to a collective action problem, potentially causing AI companies to under-invest in safety. We hope these strategies will encourage greater cooperation on the safe development of AI and lead to better global outcomes of AI.

items.title: OpenAI Robotics Symposium 2019
items.summary: We hosted the first OpenAI Robotics Symposium on April 27, 2019.

items.title: OpenAI Scholars 2019: Final projects
items.summary: Our second class of OpenAI Scholars has concluded, with all eight scholars producing an exciting final project showcased at Scholars Demo Day at OpenAI.

items.title: OpenAI Fellows Fall 2018: Final projects
items.summary: Our second class of OpenAI Fellows has wrapped up, with each Fellow going from a machine learning beginner to core OpenAI contributor in the course of a 6-month apprenticeship. We are currently reviewing applications on a rolling basis for our next round of OpenAI Fellows Summer 2019.

items.title: Transfer of adversarial robustness between perturbation types
MuseNet
items.summary: We’ve created MuseNet, a deep neural network that can generate 4-minute musical compositions with 10 different instruments, and can combine styles from country to Mozart to the Beatles. MuseNet was not explicitly programmed with our understanding of music, but instead discovered patterns of harmony, rhythm, and style by learning to predict the next token in hundreds of thousands of MIDI files. MuseNet uses the same general-purpose unsupervised technology as GPT-2, a large-scale transformer model trained to predict the next token in a sequence, whether audio or text.

items.title: Generative modeling with sparse transformers
items.summary: We’ve developed the Sparse Transformer, a deep neural network which sets new records at predicting what comes next in a sequence—whether text, images, or sound. It uses an algorithmic improvement of the attention mechanism to extract patterns from sequences 30x longer than possible previously.

items.title: OpenAI Five defeats Dota 2 world champions
items.summary: OpenAI Five is the first AI to beat the world champions in an esports game, having won two back-to-back games versus the world champion Dota 2 team, OG, at Finals this weekend. Both OpenAI Five and DeepMind’s AlphaStar had previously beaten good pros privately but lost their live pro matches, making this also the first time an AI has beaten esports pros on livestream.

items.title: OpenAI Five Finals
items.summary: We’ll be holding our final live event for OpenAI Five at 11:30am PT on April 13.

items.title: Implicit generation and generalization methods for energy-based models
items.summary: We’ve made progress towards stable and scalable training of energy-based models (EBMs) resulting in better sample quality and generalization ability than existing models. Generation in EBMs spends more compute to continually refine its answers and doing so can generate samples competitive with GANs at low temperatures, while also having mode coverage guarantees of likelihood-based models. We hope these findings stimulate further research into this promising class of models.

items.title: OpenAI Scholars 2019: Meet our Scholars
items.summary: Our class of eight scholars (out of 550 applicants) brings together collective expertise in literature, philosophy, cell biology, statistics, economics, quantum physics, and business innovation.

items.title: OpenAI LP
items.summary: We’ve created OpenAI LP, a new “capped-profit” company that allows us to rapidly increase our investments in compute and talent while including checks and balances to actualize our mission.

items.title: Introducing Activation Atlases
items.summary: We’ve created activation atlases (in collaboration with Google researchers), a new technique for visualizing what interactions between neurons can represent. As AI systems are deployed in increasingly sensitive contexts, having a better understanding of their internal decision-making processes will let us identify weaknesses and investigate failures.

items.title: Neural MMO: A massively multiagent game environment
items.summary: We’re releasing a Neural MMO, a massively multiagent game environment for reinforcement learning agents. Our platform supports a large, variable number of agents within a persistent and open-ended task. The inclusion of many agents and species leads to better exploration, divergent niche formation, and greater overall competence.

items.title: Spinning Up in Deep RL: Workshop review
items.summary: On February 2, we held our first Spinning Up Workshop as part of our new education initiative at OpenAI.

items.title: AI safety needs social scientists
items.summary: We’ve written a paper arguing that long-term AI safety research needs social scientists to ensure AI alignment algorithms succeed when actual humans are involved. Properly aligning advanced AI systems with human values requires resolving many uncertainties related to the psychology of human rationality, emotion, and biases. The aim of this paper is to spark further collaboration between machine learning and social science researchers, and we plan to hire social scientists to work on this full time at OpenAI.

items.title: Better language models and their implications
items.summary: We’ve trained a large-scale unsupervised language model which generates coherent paragraphs of text, achieves state-of-the-art performance on many language modeling benchmarks, and performs rudimentary reading comprehension, machine translation, question answering, and summarization—all without task-specific training.

items.title: Computational limitations in robust classification and win-win results
OpenAI Fellows Summer 2018: Final projects
items.summary: Our first cohort of OpenAI Fellows has concluded, with each Fellow going from a machine learning beginner to core OpenAI contributor in the course of a 6-month apprenticeship.

items.title: How AI training scales
items.summary: We’ve discovered that the gradient noise scale, a simple statistical metric, predicts the parallelizability of neural network training on a wide range of tasks. Since complex tasks tend to have noisier gradients, increasingly large batch sizes are likely to become useful in the future, removing one potential limit to further growth of AI systems. More broadly, these results show that neural network training need not be considered a mysterious art, but can be rigorized and systematized.

items.title: Quantifying generalization in reinforcement learning
items.summary: We’re releasing CoinRun, a training environment which provides a metric for an agent’s ability to transfer its experience to novel situations and has already helped clarify a longstanding puzzle in reinforcement learning. CoinRun strikes a desirable balance in complexity: the environment is simpler than traditional platformer games like Sonic the Hedgehog but still poses a worthy generalization challenge for state of the art algorithms.

items.title: Spinning Up in Deep RL
items.summary: We’re releasing Spinning Up in Deep RL, an educational resource designed to let anyone learn to become a skilled practitioner in deep reinforcement learning. Spinning Up consists of crystal-clear examples of RL code, educational exercises, documentation, and tutorials.

items.title: Learning concepts with energy functions
items.summary: We’ve developed an energy-based model that can quickly learn to identify and generate instances of concepts, such as near, above, between, closest, and furthest, expressed as sets of 2d points. Our model learns these concepts after only five demonstrations. We also show cross-domain transfer: we use concepts learned in a 2d particle environment to solve tasks on a 3-dimensional physics-based robot.

items.title: Plan online, learn offline: Efficient learning and exploration via model-based control
Reinforcement learning with prediction-based rewards
items.summary: We’ve developed Random Network Distillation (RND), a prediction-based method for encouraging reinforcement learning agents to explore their environments through curiosity, which for the first time exceeds average human performance on Montezuma’s Revenge.

items.title: Learning complex goals with iterated amplification
items.summary: We’re proposing an AI safety technique called iterated amplification that lets us specify complicated behaviors and goals that are beyond human scale, by demonstrating how to decompose a task into simpler sub-tasks, rather than by providing labeled data or a reward function. Although this idea is in its very early stages and we have only completed experiments on simple toy algorithmic domains, we’ve decided to present it in its preliminary state because we think it could prove to be a scalable approach to AI safety.

items.title: OpenAI Scholars 2019: Applications open
items.summary: We are now accepting applications for our second cohort of OpenAI Scholars, a program where we provide 6–10 stipends and mentorship to individuals from underrepresented groups to study deep learning full-time for 3 months and open-source a project.

items.title: OpenAI Fellows Winter 2019 & Interns Summer 2019
items.summary: We are now accepting applications for OpenAI Fellows and Interns for 2019.

items.title: FFJORD: Free-form continuous dynamics for scalable reversible generative models
OpenAI Scholars 2018: Final projects
items.summary: Our first cohort of OpenAI Scholars has now completed the program.

items.title: The International 2018: Results
items.summary: OpenAI Five lost two games against top Dota 2 players at The International in Vancouver this week, maintaining a good chance of winning for the first 20–35 minutes of both games.

items.title: Large-scale study of curiosity-driven learning
OpenAI Five Benchmark: Results
items.summary: Yesterday, OpenAI Five won a best-of-three against a team of 99.95th percentile Dota players: Blitz, Cap, Fogged, Merlini, and MoonMeander—four of whom have played Dota professionally—in front of a live audience and 100,000 concurrent livestream viewers.

items.title: Learning dexterity
items.summary: We’ve trained a human-like robot hand to manipulate physical objects with unprecedented dexterity.

items.title: Variational option discovery algorithms
OpenAI Scholars 2018: Meet our Scholars
items.summary: Our first class of OpenAI Scholars is underway, and you can now follow along as this group of experienced software developers becomes machine learning practitioners.

items.title: OpenAI Five Benchmark
items.summary: The OpenAI Five Benchmark match is now over!

items.title: Glow: Better reversible generative models
items.summary: We introduce Glow, a reversible generative model which uses invertible 1x1 convolutions. It extends previous work on reversible generative models and simplifies the architecture. Our model can generate realistic high resolution images, supports efficient sampling, and discovers features that can be used to manipulate attributes of data. We’re releasing code for the model and an online visualization tool so people can explore and build on these results.

items.title: Learning Montezuma’s Revenge from a single demonstration
items.summary: We’ve trained an agent to achieve a high score of 74,500 on Montezuma’s Revenge from a single human demonstration, better than any previously published result. Our algorithm is simple: the agent plays a sequence of games starting from carefully chosen states from the demonstration, and learns from them by optimizing the game score using PPO, the same reinforcement learning algorithm that underpins OpenAI Five.

items.title: OpenAI Five
items.summary: Our team of five neural networks, OpenAI Five, has started to defeat amateur human teams at Dota 2.

items.title: Retro Contest: Results
items.summary: The first run of our Retro Contest—exploring the development of algorithms that can generalize from previous experience—is now complete.

items.title: Learning policy representations in multiagent systems
Improving language understanding with unsupervised learning
items.summary: We’ve obtained state-of-the-art results on a suite of diverse language tasks with a scalable, task-agnostic system, which we’re also releasing. Our approach is a combination of two existing ideas: transformers and unsupervised pre-training. These results provide a convincing example that pairing supervised learning methods with unsupervised pre-training works very well; this is an idea that many have explored in the past, and we hope our result motivates further research into applying this idea on larger and more diverse datasets.

items.title: GamePad: A learning environment for theorem proving
OpenAI Fellows Fall 2018
items.summary: We’re now accepting applications for the next cohort of OpenAI Fellows, a program which offers a compensated 6-month apprenticeship in AI research at OpenAI.

items.title: Gym Retro
items.summary: We’re releasing the full version of Gym Retro, a platform for reinforcement learning research on games. This brings our publicly-released game count from around 70 Atari games and 30 Sega games to over 1,000 games across a variety of backing emulators. We’re also releasing the tool we use to add new games to the platform.

items.title: AI and compute
items.summary: We’re releasing an analysis showing that since 2012, the amount of compute used in the largest AI training runs has been increasing exponentially with a 3.4-month doubling time (by comparison, Moore’s Law had a 2-year doubling period)[^footnote-correction]. Since 2012, this metric has grown by more than 300,000x (a 2-year doubling period would yield only a 7x increase). Improvements in compute have been a key component of AI progress, so as long as this trend continues, it’s worth preparing for the implications of systems far outside today’s capabilities.

items.title: AI safety via debate
items.summary: We’re proposing an AI safety technique which trains agents to debate topics with one another, using a human to judge who wins.

items.title: Evolved Policy Gradients
items.summary: We’re releasing an experimental metalearning approach called Evolved Policy Gradients, a method that evolves the loss function of learning agents, which can enable fast training on novel tasks. Agents trained with EPG can succeed at basic tasks at test time that were outside their training regime, like learning to navigate to an object on a different side of the room from where it was placed during training.

items.title: Gotta Learn Fast: A new benchmark for generalization in RL
Retro Contest
items.summary: We’re launching a transfer learning contest that measures a reinforcement learning algorithm’s ability to generalize from previous experience.

items.title: Variance reduction for policy gradient with action-dependent factorized baselines
Report from the OpenAI hackathon
items.summary: On March 3rd, we hosted our first hackathon with 100 members of the artificial intelligence community.

items.title: Improving GANs using optimal transport
On first-order meta-learning algorithms
Reptile: A scalable meta-learning algorithm
items.summary: We’ve developed a simple meta-learning algorithm called Reptile which works by repeatedly sampling a task, performing stochastic gradient descent on it, and updating the initial parameters towards the final parameters learned on that task. Reptile is the application of the Shortest Descent algorithm to the meta-learning setting, and is mathematically similar to first-order MAML (which is a version of the well-known MAML algorithm) that only needs black-box access to an optimizer such as SGD or Adam, with similar computational efficiency and performance.

items.title: OpenAI Scholars
items.summary: We’re providing 6–10 stipends and mentorship to individuals from underrepresented groups to study deep learning full-time for 3 months and open-source a project.

items.title: Some considerations on learning to explore via meta-reinforcement learning
Ingredients for robotics research
items.summary: We’re releasing eight simulated robotics environments and a Baselines implementation of Hindsight Experience Replay, all developed for our research over the past year. We’ve used these environments to train models which work on physical robots. We’re also releasing a set of requests for robotics research.

items.title: Multi-Goal Reinforcement Learning: Challenging robotics environments and request for research
OpenAI hackathon
items.summary: Come to OpenAI’s office in San Francisco’s Mission District for talks and a hackathon on Saturday, March 3rd.

items.title: OpenAI supporters
items.summary: We’re excited to welcome new donors to OpenAI.

items.title: Preparing for malicious uses of AI
items.summary: We’ve co-authored a paper that forecasts how malicious actors could misuse AI technology, and potential ways we can prevent and mitigate these threats. This paper is the outcome of almost a year of sustained work with our colleagues at the Future of Humanity Institute, the Centre for the Study of Existential Risk, the Center for a New American Security, the Electronic Frontier Foundation, and others.

items.title: Interpretable machine learning through teaching
items.summary: We’ve designed a method that encourages AIs to teach each other with examples that also make sense to humans. Our approach automatically selects the most informative examples to teach a concept—for instance, the best images to describe the concept of dogs—and experimentally we found our approach to be effective at teaching both AIs

items.title: Discovering types for entity disambiguation
items.summary: We’ve built a system for automatically figuring out which object is meant by a word by having a neural network decide if the word belongs to each of about 100 automatically-discovered “types” (non-exclusive categories).

items.title: Requests for Research 2.0
items.summary: We’re releasing a new batch of seven unsolved problems which have come up in the course of our research at OpenAI.

items.title: Scaling Kubernetes to 2,500 nodes
Block-sparse GPU kernels
items.summary: We’re releasing highly-optimized GPU kernels for an underexplored class of neural network architectures: networks with block-sparse weights. Depending on the chosen sparsity, these kernels can run orders of magnitude faster than cuBLAS or cuSPARSE. We’ve used them to attain state-of-the-art results in text sentiment analysis and generative modeling of text and images.

items.title: Learning sparse neural networks through L₀ regularization
Interpretable and pedagogical examples
Learning a hierarchy
items.summary: We’ve developed a hierarchical reinforcement learning algorithm that learns high-level actions useful for solving a range of tasks, allowing fast solving of tasks requiring thousands of timesteps. Our algorithm, when applied to a set of navigation problems, discovers a set of high-level actions for walking and crawling in different directions, which enables the agent to master new navigation tasks quickly.

items.title: Generalizing from simulation
items.summary: Our latest robotics techniques allow robot controllers, trained entirely in simulation and deployed on physical robots, to react to unplanned changes in the environment as they solve simple tasks. That is, we’ve used these techniques to build closed-loop systems rather than open-loop ones as before.

items.title: Sim-to-real transfer of robotic control with dynamics randomization
Asymmetric actor critic for image-based robot learning
Domain randomization and generative models for robotic grasping
Competitive self-play
items.summary: We’ve found that self-play allows simulated AIs to discover physical skills like tackling, ducking, faking, kicking, catching, and diving for the ball, without explicitly designing an environment with these skills in mind. Self-play ensures that the environment is always the right difficulty for an AI to improve. Taken alongside our Dota 2 self-play results, we have increasing confidence that self-play will be a core part of powerful AI systems in the future.

items.title: Meta-learning for wrestling
items.summary: We show that for the task of simulated robot wrestling, a meta-learning agent can learn to quickly defeat a stronger non-meta-learning agent, and also show that the meta-learning agent can adapt to physical malfunction.

items.title: Nonlinear computation in deep linear networks
Learning to model other minds
items.summary: We’re releasing an algorithm which accounts for the fact that other agents are learning too, and discovers self-interested yet collaborative strategies like tit-for-tat in the iterated prisoner’s dilemma. This algorithm, Learning with Opponent-Learning Awareness (LOLA), is a small step towards agents that model other minds.

items.title: Learning with opponent-learning awareness
OpenAI Baselines: ACKTR & A2C
items.summary: We’re releasing two new OpenAI Baselines implementations: ACKTR and A2C. A2C is a synchronous, deterministic variant of Asynchronous Advantage Actor Critic (A3C) which we’ve found gives equal performance. ACKTR is a more sample-efficient reinforcement learning algorithm than TRPO and A2C, and requires only slightly more computation than A2C per update.

items.title: More on Dota 2
items.summary: Our Dota 2 result shows that self-play can catapult the performance of machine learning systems from far below human level to superhuman, given sufficient compute. In the span of a month, our system went from barely matching a high-ranked player to beating the top pros and has continued to improve since then. Supervised deep learning systems can only be as good as their training datasets, but in self-play systems, the available data improves automatically as the agent gets better.

items.title: Dota 2
items.summary: We’ve created a bot which beats the world’s top professionals at 1v1 matches of Dota 2 under standard tournament rules. The bot learned the game from scratch by self-play, and does not use imitation learning or tree search. This is a step towards building AI systems which accomplish well-defined goals in messy, complicated situations involving real humans.

items.title: Gathering human feedback
items.summary: RL-Teacher is an open-source implementation of our interface to train AIs via occasional human feedback rather than hand-crafted reward functions. The underlying technique was developed as a step towards safe AI systems, but also applies to reinforcement learning problems with rewards that are hard to specify.

items.title: Better exploration with parameter noise
items.summary: We’ve found that adding adaptive noise to the parameters of reinforcement learning algorithms frequently boosts performance. This exploration method is simple to implement and very rarely decreases performance, so it’s worth trying on any problem.

items.title: Proximal Policy Optimization
items.summary: We’re releasing a new class of reinforcement learning algorithms, Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), which perform comparably or better than state-of-the-art approaches while being much simpler to implement and tune. PPO has become the default reinforcement learning algorithm at OpenAI because of its ease of use and good performance.

items.title: Robust adversarial inputs
items.summary: We’ve created images that reliably fool neural network classifiers when viewed from varied scales and perspectives. This challenges a claim from last week that self-driving cars would be hard to trick maliciously since they capture images from multiple scales, angles, perspectives, and the like.

items.title: Hindsight Experience Replay
Teacher–student curriculum learning
Faster physics in Python
items.summary: We’re open-sourcing a high-performance Python library for robotic simulation using the MuJoCo engine, developed over our past year of robotics research.

items.title: Learning from human preferences
items.summary: One step towards building safe AI systems is to remove the need for humans to write goal functions, since using a simple proxy for a complex goal, or getting the complex goal a bit wrong, can lead to undesirable and even dangerous behavior. In collaboration with DeepMind’s safety team, we’ve developed an algorithm which can infer what humans want by being told which of two proposed behaviors is better.

items.title: Learning to cooperate, compete, and communicate
items.summary: Multiagent environments where agents compete for resources are stepping stones on the path to AGI. Multiagent environments have two useful properties: first, there is a natural curriculum—the difficulty of the environment is determined by the skill of your competitors (and if you’re competing against clones of yourself, the environment exactly matches your skill level). Second, a multiagent environment has no stable equilibrium: no matter how smart an agent is, there’s always pressure to get smarter. These environments have a very different feel from traditional environments, and it’ll take a lot more research before we become good at them.

items.title: UCB exploration via Q-ensembles
OpenAI Baselines: DQN
items.summary: We’re open-sourcing OpenAI Baselines, our internal effort to reproduce reinforcement learning algorithms with performance on par with published results. We’ll release the algorithms over upcoming months; today’s release includes DQN and three of its variants.

items.title: Robots that learn
items.summary: We’ve created a robotics system, trained entirely in simulation and deployed on a physical robot, which can learn a new task after seeing it done once.

items.title: Roboschool
items.summary: We are releasing Roboschool: open-source software for robot simulation, integrated with OpenAI Gym.

items.title: Equivalence between policy gradients and soft Q-learning
Stochastic Neural Networks for hierarchical reinforcement learning
Unsupervised sentiment neuron
items.summary: We’ve developed an unsupervised system which learns an excellent representation of sentiment, despite being trained only to predict the next character in the text of Amazon reviews.

items.title: Spam detection in the physical world
items.summary: We’ve created the world’s first Spam-detecting AI trained entirely in simulation and deployed on a physical robot.

items.title: Evolution strategies as a scalable alternative to reinforcement learning
items.summary: We’ve discovered that evolution strategies (ES), an optimization technique that’s been known for decades, rivals the performance of standard reinforcement learning (RL) techniques on modern RL benchmarks (e.g. Atari/MuJoCo), while overcoming many of RL’s inconveniences.

items.title: One-shot imitation learning
Distill
items.summary: We’re excited to support today’s launch of Distill, a new kind of journal aimed at excellent communication of machine learning results (novel or existing).

items.title: Learning to communicate
items.summary: In this post we’ll outline new OpenAI research in which agents develop their own language.

items.title: Emergence of grounded compositional language in multi-agent populations
Prediction and control with temporal segment models
Third-person imitation learning
Attacking machine learning with adversarial examples
items.summary: Adversarial examples are inputs to machine learning models that an attacker has intentionally designed to cause the model to make a mistake; they’re like optical illusions for machines. In this post we’ll show how adversarial examples work across different mediums, and will discuss why securing systems against them can be difficult.

items.title: Adversarial attacks on neural network policies
Team update
items.summary: The OpenAI team is now 45 people. Together, we’re pushing the frontier of AI capabilities—whether by validating novel ideas, creating new software systems, or deploying machine learning on robots.

items.title: PixelCNN++: Improving the PixelCNN with discretized logistic mixture likelihood and other modifications
Faulty reward functions in the wild
items.summary: Reinforcement learning algorithms can break in surprising, counterintuitive ways. In this post we’ll explore one failure mode, which is where you misspecify your reward function.

items.title: Universe
items.summary: We’re releasing Universe, a software platform for measuring and training an AI’s general intelligence across the world’s supply of games, websites and other applications.

items.title: OpenAI and Microsoft
items.summary: We’re working with Microsoft to start running most of our large-scale experiments on Azure.

items.title: #Exploration: A study of count-based exploration for deep reinforcement learning
On the quantitative analysis of decoder-based generative models
A connection between generative adversarial networks, inverse reinforcement learning, and energy-based models
RL²: Fast reinforcement learning via slow reinforcement learning
Variational lossy autoencoder
Extensions and limitations of the neural GPU
Semi-supervised knowledge transfer for deep learning from private training data
Report from the self-organizing conference
items.summary: Last week we hosted over a hundred and fifty AI practitioners in our offices for our first self-organizing conference on machine learning.

items.title: commit-rewriter 0.1
items.summary: Release: commit-rewriter 0.1 I built this little web app the other day to help edit the commit messages for the Datasette security releases . The initial commits were full of coding agent cruft and references to issue IDs from our private repository, so they weren't fit for publication. If you want to edit the commit messages for a repository you can run it like this: uvx commit-rewriter path/to/repo Omit the path if you are already in the directory for that repo. When you submit your edits the tool creates a timestamped branch of your current repo state - to allow you to revert if you need to - and then rewrites every commit from the first one you edited to the most recent. items.title: OpenAI GPT-6 Astra 现已在 Amazon Bedrock 上正式推出
items.summary: 今天，AWS 宣布在 Amazon Bedrock 上正式推出 OpenAI 的 GPT-6 Astra。GPT-6 Astra 是 OpenAI 迄今为止最新、功能最强大的模型，可为要求严苛的业务工作流提供更深入的推理与判断能力、专业水准的写作与设计能力，以及先进的计算机和浏览器使用能力。它支持最多 100 万个输入 Token 的上下文窗口，并且可以生成符合组织基调、模板和标准的输出。Amazon Bedrock 推理引擎提供生产工作负载所需的性能、安全性和规模。 您可以通过受支持的 Amazon Bedrock API 直接调用 GPT-6 Astra，也可以配置 ChatGPT Work 和 Codex 以在 Amazon Bedrock 上使用该模型。使用它来构建自主智能体、分析大量文档集合、调查复杂的软件问题，以及创建需要在相互竞争的输入之间做出判断的应用程序。作为此次发布的一部分，OpenAI 还推出了适用于 ChatGPT Work 的新企业插件，这些插件将 Astra 的浏览器使用能力扩展到了常见的业务应用程序中。完善的 AWS 控制措施可帮助您保护工作负载、管理访问权限和审计模型调用活动。 您可以在 Amazon Bedrock 控制台 或通过 Amazon Bedrock API（以编程方式）开始使用。有关支持的 AWS 区域 、端点、API、功能、推理配置文件和定价的信息，请参阅 Amazon Bedrock 文档 。 要了解可使用 GPT-6 Astra 构建的内容，请阅读 博客 。

items.title: 适用于 InfluxDB 的 Amazon Timestream 现在支持自定义插件
items.summary: 适用于 InfluxDB 的 Amazon Timestream 现支持在 InfluxDB 3 Core 和企业版的托管版本上运行自定义 Python 插件。您将插件代码托管在您所控制的公有或私有存储库中，引擎会根据触发器获取并运行该代码，从而让您无需搭建独立的外部基础设施，即可实施针对特定工作负载的逻辑。 插件可在处理引擎已支持的触发器类型上运行，借助这些插件，您可以构建自定义数据转换、警报、聚合以及与自有服务的集成，所有这些均在数据附近运行。插件在托管的 Python 环境中运行，该环境包含标准库和经过 Amazon 审核的软件包，因此您可以将特定于工作负载的处理转移到数据库中，而无需为此运行单独的管道。 要开始使用，请在数据库参数组中设置一个插件存储库，将该参数组应用到集群，并使用 influxdb3 CLI 或 HTTP API 创建引用该插件的触发器；私有存储库通过存储在 AWS Secrets Manager 中的令牌进行身份验证。 自定义插件已在提供适用于 InfluxDB 的 Amazon Timestream 的所有 AWS 区域 推出。要开始使用适用于 InfluxDB 3 的 Amazon Timestream，请访问 适用于 InfluxDB 的 Amazon Timestream 控制台 。有关更多信息，请参阅 适用于 InfluxDB 的 Amazon Timestream 文档 和 定价页面 。

items.title: Amazon SageMaker Feature Store 现在支持单个特征更新以降低写入延迟
items.summary: Amazon SageMaker Feature Store 是一项完全托管的功能，可用于轻松计算、存储和检索用于训练和部署人工智能模型的特征。SageMaker Feature Store 现已支持特征级写入，这是一项用于更新记录中单个特征的新功能。数据科学家现在可以在单个请求中更新一个或多个特征值，而无需重写整个记录。 数据科学家可以使用一次更新调用来替换其管道目前运行的读取-修改-写入模式。每次写入仅更新请求中的特征，而记录中的其他特征保持不变，从而降低写入延迟和成本。当多个管道向同一特征组写入数据时，每个管道仅更新其计算的特征，因此流式处理作业和夜间批处理作业可以独立更新同一条记录。这项功能使数据科学家能够在高处理量下更新单个特征，而无需在数据摄取管道中构建合并逻辑。 此功能已在提供 Amazon SageMaker Feature Store 的所有 AWS 区域 推出。有关更多信息，请参阅 Amazon Feature Store Runtime 、 标准 V2 文档 和 发布博客 。

items.title: AWS Transform 现已在 AWS GovCloud（美国西部）推出
items.summary: AWS Transform 现已在 AWS GovCloud（美国西部）区域推出，使政府机构和监管组织能够规划和执行向 AWS 的大规模迁移。此次发布后，在 AWS GovCloud（美国）运营的客户现在可以利用 AWS Transform 的 迁移功能 ，在专为托管敏感数据和受监管工作负载而设计的隔离环境中，自动完成服务器迁移。该区域的 AWS Transform 支持将服务器迁移至 AWS GovCloud（美国东部）和 AWS GovCloud（美国西部）作为 目标区域 。 迁移 VMware、裸机、Hyper-V 或数据库工作负载的组织可以使用 AWS Transform 自动复制和切换服务器，从而减少大规模迁移所涉及的手动工作和风险。这对于必须在 AWS GovCloud（美国）边界内运营的联邦机构、国防承包商和受监管行业来说尤为重要。此次区域发布不包含现代化、自定义转换和评测功能，这些功能在受支持的商用区域中仍可用。 要开始使用，请参阅 AWS Transform 文档 或访问 AWS Transform 产品页面 。

items.title: Amazon API Gateway 现在支持将双向 TLS 用于后端集成
items.summary: 您现在可以配置 Amazon API Gateway REST API，以在 TLS 握手过程中向后端提供 AWS Certificate Manager（ACM）证书，从而启用双向 TLS（mTLS）。以前，API Gateway 只能提供其生成的自签名证书；现在，您可以使用由您信任的证书颁发机构签名的证书。您的集成端点将在握手过程中验证此证书，以确认连接来自您的 API。 您可以将证书从现有的公有密钥基础设施（PKI）导入 ACM，也可以让 ACM 通过 AWS 私有证书颁发机构为您签发并管理证书。当在 ACM 中重新导入或续订证书时，API Gateway 会自动传播该更新，无需重新部署，也不会造成停机。结合现有的针对客户端连接的入站 mTLS 支持，您可以在客户端到 API 以及 API 到后端的连接中应用双向身份验证，这是金融服务、医疗保健行业以及其他受监管或零信任环境中的常见要求。 用于后端集成的双向 TLS 已在提供 API Gateway REST API 的所有 AWS 商业区域和 AWS GovCloud（美国）区域推出。您可以通过 API Gateway 控制台、AWS CLI 或 AWS CloudFormation 对其进行配置。要开始使用，请参阅 Amazon API Gateway 文档 和 AWS 博客文章 。

items.title: Amazon RDS for MariaDB 现在支持社区 MariaDB 次要版本 10.6.28、10.11.19、11.4.13、11.8.9 和 12.3.3
items.summary: 即日起， Amazon Relational Database Service（Amazon RDS）for MariaDB 支持 MariaDB 次要版本 10.6.28、10.11.19、11.4.13、11.8.9 和 12.3.3，这是 MariaDB 社区发布的最新次要版本。除了操作方面的改进外，这些次要版本还引入了对后量子 TLS（PQ-TLS）密钥交换的支持，为您提供了用于加密传输中数据的后量子密码学选项。建议您升级到更新的次要版本，以修复早期 MariaDB 版本中的常见漏洞和泄露（CVE），并享受漏洞修复、性能改进及 MariaDB 社区增加的新功能带来的好处。有关 RDS for MariaDB 中改进的更多信息，请参阅 RDS MariaDB 发行说明 。 您可以使用 Amazon RDS 蓝绿部署 、就地升级或从快照还原来升级数据库。要大规模简化操作，请启用 自动次要版本升级 ，并使用 AWS Organizations 升级部署策略 以分阶段编排集群升级。有关执行版本升级的更多信息，请参阅 Amazon RDS 用户指南 。您还可以使用 AWS Database Migration Service ，从外部 MariaDB 源迁移到 RDS for MariaDB。有关定价详细信息和区域可用性，请参阅 Amazon RDS for MariaDB 。 Amazon RDS for MariaDB 可让您轻松地在云中设置、操作和扩展 MariaDB 部署。在 Amazon RDS 管理控制台 中创建或更新完全托管式 Amazon RDS for MariaDB 数据库。

items.title: AWS HealthOmics 推出适用于 WDL 工作流的资源回退顺序
items.summary: 今天，AWS HealthOmics 推出资源回退指令，使您能够为工作流描述语言（WDL）工作流中的任务定义一组有序的首选加速器类型列表，其中包括一个回退至 CPU 实例的选项。研究人员和生物信息学家可以利用此指令，减少因加速器限制而诊断和重新提交运行所花费的时间，并确保生产工作流的持续运行。 AWS HealthOmics 是一项符合 HIPAA 标准的服务，能够通过完全托管式生物信息学工作流，帮助医疗保健与生命科学客户大规模加速取得科学突破。 利用资源回退功能，您可以为任务优先使用首选加速器。当首选加速器不可用时，HealthOmics 会自动按照您在回退策略中指定的顺序依次尝试其他选项，而无需重新提交。每个加速器配置文件都有可配置的超时时间，使您可以控制 HealthOmics 在尝试下一个加速器之前搜索该加速器的时间。较短的超时时间有助于快速遍历回退顺序，而较长的超时时间会增加预留首选加速器的可能性。您还可以将 CPU 配置文件作为最后的回退策略，以增加任务预留实例的可能性。 您现在可以在支持 AWS HealthOmics 的所有区域使用适用于 WDL 工作流的资源回退功能：美国东部（弗吉尼亚州北部、俄亥俄州）、美国西部（俄勒冈州）、欧洲地区（法兰克福、爱尔兰、伦敦）、以色列（特拉维夫）和亚太地区（首尔、新加坡、东京）。要了解更多信息，请访问 高级资源配置文档 。

items.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory 现在支持直接摄取到长期记忆
items.summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory 现在支持开发人员直接提交内容以供长期记忆提取，无需将其作为短期记忆事件保存。新的 IngestData API 会接受内容，将其扇出到记忆中配置好的长期记忆策略中，并通过与用于任何其他长期记忆记录相同的检索操作提供生成的记忆记录，且整个过程不会创建短期事件。 到目前为止，所有内容都必须先作为短期记忆事件进行存储，然后提取策略才能将其处理成长期记忆记录。IngestData 消除了这一要求，使开发人员能够独立于短期记忆来采用长期记忆。 IngestData 同时支持对话型有效载荷（具有 USER/ASSISTANT 角色的消息）和 JSON 有效载荷（行为事件、活动日志、系统事件），并接受可选元数据，这些元数据会输入到与 CreateEvent 相同的提取管道中。处理后，开发人员可以使用 ListMemoryRecords 或 RetrieveMemoryRecords 验证提取结果，通过 Kinesis 流式传输实时通知，并使用 ListMemoryExtractionJobs 重启失败的提取。要开始使用，请参阅《Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 开发人员指南》中的 直接摄取到长期记忆 。IngestData 已在支持 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory 的所有 AWS 区域推出。

items.title: AWS 宣布推出用于搭建全栈应用程序的 Nx Plugin for AWS
items.summary: Nx Plugin for AWS 版本 1.0 现已推出，这是一款用于在 AWS 上搭建全栈应用程序的开源工具包。人工智能助手可以在几分钟内在 AWS 上搭建好应用程序，但很少能一次性就将安全性、可观测性和类型安全性都处理妥当。该插件扩展了 Nx（一个面向单存储库的、与语言无关的开源构建系统），其生成器可在收到请求时分别构建应用程序的某个部分，并同时构建运行该部分所需的基础设施。 生成器涵盖 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 上的智能体和模型上下文协议服务器，以及基于 TypeScript 和 Python 中经过验证的开源框架构建的 API、网站和数据库。每个生成器都会生成应用程序中一个可运行且可部署的组件，并将基础设施定义为 AWS Cloud Development Kit（AWS CDK）构造或 Terraform 模块，同时遵循最佳实践，例如启用 AWS WAF 保护、将访问日志记录到 Amazon CloudWatch 以及使用 AWS X-Ray 追踪。连接生成器会将项目与类型安全的客户端进行绑定，因此，当 API 发生破坏性变更时，会触发构建错误，而非在生产环境中导致请求失败。 每个生成器每次都能产生相同的结果，从而为人工智能助手提供可靠的基础。生成的代码归您所有，运行时不依赖该插件，而且 Nx 迁移会将后续的改进应用到您自定义的工作区中。 该插件随 Apache 2.0 许可证提供，无需额外付费；您只需为应用程序使用的 AWS 资源付费。要了解更多信息，请参阅 发布博客文章 和 文档 。

items.title: AWS 构建者 ID 为第三方登录增加了恢复选项和多重身份验证功能
items.summary: AWS 构建者 ID 是您访问包括 AWS Builder Center、AWS Training and Certification、Amazon Quick 以及 Kiro 在内的 AWS 应用程序的个人配置文件，现在提供新的方式来保护和恢复您的个人配置文件。您可以添加一个恢复电子邮件地址，并使用新的自助服务选项，以便在被锁定时重新获得访问权限。您还可以为任何登录方式注册多重身份验证（MFA）设备，包括 Google 或 Apple 等第三方登录方式。 通过这些增强功能，您可以获得更多自助服务选项来恢复 AWS 构建者 ID。添加恢复电子邮件地址提供了第二个验证因素，无需联系 AWS Support 即可在更多情况下进行自助恢复。您可以使用发送到您的主要电子邮件地址或恢复电子邮件地址的链接来重置忘记的密码。如果您无法访问 MFA 设备，则可以通过验证主要电子邮件地址和恢复电子邮件地址来重新获得访问权限。如果您使用 Google、Apple、GitHub 或 Amazon 登录 Builder ID，现在可以直接在 AWS 构建者 ID 中注册 MFA 设备，从而获得与此前使用电子邮件地址和密码的用户相同的强账户保护；此外，如果您无法访问第三方账户，还可以将登录方式永久切换为电子邮件地址和密码。 要了解有关 AWS 构建者 ID 以及如何设置账户恢复和 MFA 的更多信息，请访问 AWS Builder ID 文档 。

items.title: What blog posts influenced your thinking the most?
items.summary: My comment on What blog posts influenced your thinking the most? — Lobste.rs. An early Joel Spolsky one for me was The Law of Leaky Abstractions . I read that near the start of my career and it's encouraged me to always be looking for improved understanding of the layers under where I'm working, just in case one of those abstractions leaks. A more recent one, from 2018, is Migrations: the sole scalable fix to tech debt by Will Larson. I absolutely love his idea that migrations (e.g. replacing one service with a new one, or switching database engines, or whatever) are part and parcel of software engineering and are a skill that you should invest in and get good at, not avoid or treat as special one-offs. The Engineer/Manager Pendulum by Charity Majors was hugely influential for me. I was stuck in engineering management and worried that if I switched back to being an "Individual Contributor" (ugh I hate that term) I'd damage my career. Charity gave me permission to make the switch by pointing out that many of the most successful software developers pendulum from one track to the other multiple times over their career, and doing so makes you better at both sides. items.title: The contagion of fear
items.summary: The contagion of fear Bryan Cantrill responds to the tweet by former Anthropic employee Jacob Coxon confirming that many Anthropic researchers believe AI "could kill us all by the end of the decade". Bryan shares a story of his own youthful mistakes causing unjustified panic among less technical peers, and warns against doing the same: These ghoulish claims strike brazenly at the hearth, and given the obvious importance of AI, it is unsurprising that they have leapt into the mainstream, with people asking the natural question: how would that happen? The answers always rely on hand-wavy extrapolation into the future; for example, Jacob Coxon cites "hacking critical infrastructure" and "extinction-level bioweapons" without further elaboration. But Coxon is not an expert on critical infrastructure, nor on bioweapons — nor, for that matter, on extinction. [...] That said, we should not expect the public to understand LLMs, critical infrastructure, bioweapons, extinction biology, etc. — that burden must lie with those making the claim. The lesson that I learned (shamefully) decades ago is that domain experts, by way of their expertise, implicitly hold the public’s trust — and we must not abuse it. It is incumbent upon us to be circumspect in our claims — and maximally so when raising the alarm. Bryan talked about his doubts about the bioweapons concerns in the recent episode of Oxide and Friends that I joined. You can hear more of his thoughts on that starting at 51m44s in that episode. Amazon Connect Customer 现在允许您为不同类型的任务和电子邮件设置特定的容量限制
items.summary: Amazon Connect Customer 现在使联络中心经理能够为不同类型的工作设置特定的容量限制。以前，并发设置是在渠道级别应用的，因此无论复杂性或所需精力如何，都对渠道内的所有联系人一视同仁。通过此次发布，经理可以根据复杂性、优先级或业务职能，将任务和电子邮件联系人划分为不同的工作负载类型，每种类型都有各自的并发和中断规则。例如，经理可以将座席配置为同时处理最多 3 个省力的简单任务，并将需要高度关注的复杂任务限制为一次只能处理 1 个。 任务和电子邮件渠道的特定容量限制已在提供 Amazon Connect Customer 的所有 AWS 商业区域和 AWS GovCloud（美国西部） 区域 推出。要了解更多信息，请参阅 Amazon Connect Customer 管理员指南 。要了解有关 Amazon Connect Customer 的更多信息，请访问 Amazon Connect Customer 网站 。

items.title: 适用于 .NET 的 AWS Transform 现已通过 CLI 全面推出现代化改造功能
items.summary: 今天，AWS 宣布在 AWS Transform 自定义中全面推出由 AWS 托管的 .NET 现代化改造转换，只需使用一行 CLI 命令即可触发。您能够以交互方式运行此转换，也可以将其脚本化到任何现有管道或工作流中自主运行。CLI 体验补充了现有适用于 .NET 的 AWS Transform 体验：Web 应用程序、Visual Studio IDE、Kiro 能力包和 MCP 代理。 AWS Transform 自定义使组织能够利用 AWS 托管和自定义转换功能，大规模地对代码进行现代化改造和转换。您可以使用开箱即用或者可根据组织具体需求进行自定义的转换功能，来升级语言版本、迁移框架、优化性能并分析代码库。这些转换受益于持续改进，并可从每次实际使用中学习，从而能够提供更准确、更高效的结果。 AWS Transform 自定义和适用于 .NET 的 AWS Transform 已在八个 AWS 区域推出：美国东部（弗吉尼亚州北部）、亚太地区（孟买、东京、首尔、悉尼）、加拿大（中部）和欧洲地区（法兰克福、伦敦）。 .NET 现代化改造转换包含每月 50,000 分钟的免费代理分钟数。请查看“AWS Transform 定价”，了解定价详情和示例。要了解更多信息，请参阅《AWS Transform 用户指南》中的 AWS 托管的转换 。

items.title: AWS Lambda 现在支持 Lambda Managed Instances 上由 Graviton5 驱动的 EC2 实例
items.summary: AWS Lambda 现在支持 Lambda Managed Instances 上由 AWS Graviton5 驱动的 C9g、C9gd、M9g 和 M9gd 实例。现在，您可以在最新一代的 Graviton 处理器上运行 Lambda 函数，与由 Graviton4 驱动的实例相比，计算性能可以提升高达 25%。 AWS Lambda Managed Instances 使您能够在 AWS EC2 实例上运行 Lambda 函数，同时保留 Lambda 简洁的运维体验。借助 Lambda Managed Instances，您无需管理基础设施，即可获取专用计算配置，并利用 EC2 的定价优势提升成本效益。Lambda Managed Instances 全面管理所有基础设施相关任务，包括实例生命周期、操作系统及运行时补丁更新、内置路由、负载均衡，以及基于可配置参数的自动扩缩，让您能够专注于编写代码。即日起，您可以将 Lambda Managed Instances 与由 Graviton5 驱动的最新实例结合使用，与上一代由 Graviton4 驱动的实例相比，计算性能可以提升高达 25%。 要开始使用，您可以在创建容量提供程序时，指定所需的 Graviton5 实例类型（C9g、C9gd、M9g 或 M9gd）。当您将实例类型设置为默认值时，Lambda 会根据函数的配置架构、内存大小以及内存与 vCPU 的比率，自动将 Graviton5 实例纳入其选择的实例列表中。 AWS Lambda Managed Instances 支持 C9g、C9gd、M9g 和 M9gd 实例类型，该支持已在同时提供 Lambda Managed Instances 和这些 EC2 实例的所有 AWS 区域 推出。要了解更多信息，请参阅 Lambda Managed Instances 文档 和 AWS Lambda 定价 。

items.title: AWS Lambda 当前支持在 Lambda Managed Instances 上配置 90 分钟函数超时
items.summary: AWS Lambda 现在支持针对 Lambda Managed Instances（LMI） 上的 异步 和 事件源映射（ESM） 调用，配置 90 分钟函数超时，相较之前的 15 分钟限制增加了 6 倍。现在，您可以在 Lambda 上运行数据处理、媒体转码、财务计算、AI 推理和批处理工作负载，适用于需要连续执行更长时间的任务，而无需重新架构应用程序。 客户可以使用 Lambda 构建无服务器应用程序，例如事件驱动的处理器、API 后端和数据处理管道。对于需要连续执行更长时间的数据密集型工作负载，例如媒体转码、蒙特卡洛模拟等财务计算和 AI 推理，Lambda 之前的 15 分钟函数超时限制要求客户采用架构变通方案。通过今天的发布，您可以在 Lambda Managed Instances 上，针对异步和 ESM 调用配置最长 90 分钟的函数超时。Lambda Managed Instances 让您可以处理每个实例的多个并发请求、访问专用计算配置，并通过 EC2 定价优势实现成本效益，而无需管理基础设施。增加后的函数超时也适用于 Lambda 持久函数 中的调用，允许您为运行时间较长的调用设置检查点和重放步骤。异步调用时，多步持久执行可以运行长达 1 年。 您可以通过 AWS Lambda 控制台、AWS CLI、Lambda API、基础设施即代码工具或 Agent Toolkit for AWS ，为异步和 ESM 调用配置最长 90 分钟的函数超时。同步调用保留现有的最长 15 分钟超时限制。此功能已在提供 Lambda Managed Instances 的所有 AWS 区域 推出。 要了解有关配置 90 分钟函数超时的更多信息，请参阅 Lambda 开发人员指南 。要了解如何将延长超时与检查点和重放韧性相结合，请参阅 持久函数文档 。有关定价详情，请参阅 AWS Lambda 定价 。要了解有关 AWS Lambda 的更多信息，请访问 aws.amazon.com/lambda 。

items.title: Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base 新增 API 和控制台支持，用于调试文档级访问控制
items.summary: AWS 宣布推出适用于 Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base 的 CheckIngestedDocumentAcl 和 GetIngestedDocumentAcl API，为客户提供了一种自助调试文档访问问题和审计文档级权限的方式。当用户在启用了 ACL 的数据来源的检索结果中未看到预期文档时，很难确定原因是访问控制配置错误还是其他原因。这些新 API 及配套的控制台体验弥补了这一差距，使您能够快速诊断和解决权限问题，而无需提交支持案例。 CheckIngestedDocumentAcl 让您可以验证特定用户是否有权访问给定的已摄取文档，而 GetIngestedDocumentAcl 会返回附加到文档的完整 ACL，以便您准确审计配置了哪些权限并捕获配置错误。该控制台还在数据来源详细信息页面上引入了新的 Document Access Control（文档访问控制）部分，让您可以通过输入文档 ID 和用户电子邮件地址来检查访问权限，或通过文档 ID 检索文档的完整 ACL。这些功能共同为管理员提供了在企业知识库中大规模管理访问控制所需的可见性。 要了解更多信息，请参阅《Amazon Bedrock API 参考》中的 CheckIngestedDocumentAcl 和 GetIngestedDocumentAcl 。有关 Amazon Bedrock 托管知识库的更多信息，请访问 Amazon Bedrock 知识库产品页面 。

items.title: Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base 现在支持将 Confluence Data Center 作为原生数据来源连接器
items.summary: AWS 宣布针对 Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base 推出 Confluence Data Center 数据来源连接器。Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base 是一项完全托管的检索增强生成（RAG）服务。运行自托管 Confluence Data Center 实例的客户，现在可以将博客和页面从 Confluence 空间直接爬取到他们的托管知识库中。以前，将 Confluence Data Center 内容导入 Bedrock 知识库需要构建自定义数据摄取管道；现在，您只需提供实例凭证，连接器就会自动处理数据爬取、元数据提取和增量同步。 Confluence Data Center 连接器让您的智能体能够访问团队已在 Confluence 中维护的机构知识，包括跨空间的 Wiki 页面和博客文章。您可以使用过滤器将爬取范围限定为特定的空间或内容类型，确保仅摄取相关内容，使知识库保持重点突出且成本效益高。这样可以轻松地为基于工程文档、运行手册或托管在 Confluence Data Center 上的团队知识库的内部助手提供支持。 要了解更多信息，请参阅 Amazon Bedrock 用户指南 中的“Confluence Data Center 数据来源连接器”。有关 Amazon Bedrock 托管知识库的更多信息，请访问 Amazon Bedrock 知识库产品页面 。

items.title: Amazon EBS 卷克隆现在支持跨账户复制卷
items.summary: Amazon Elastic Block Store（Amazon EBS）卷克隆现在支持跨 AWS 账户复制 EBS 卷并重新加密。您可以将 EBS 卷复制到任何 AWS 账户，并使用目标账户中的 AWS Key Management Service（AWS KMS）密钥重新加密。这使将生产和开发工作负载分离到不同账户的组织，能够跨这些账户边界复制数据。 通过跨账户复制，您可以将生产数据库卷克隆到隔离的开发账户中，让开发人员获得生产数据的最新副本，以安全地进行实验。此功能还适用于需要跨环境分离加密密钥的团队，例如为生产和非生产账户维护单独的 KMS 密钥。所有卷类型都支持跨账户复制，包括未加密的卷和使用客户自主管理型密钥加密的卷。 要跨账户复制卷，您首先需要使用 AWS Resource Access Manager（AWS RAM）将该卷共享给目标账户，然后目标账户在同一可用区中创建共享卷的副本。您可以通过 AWS 管理控制台、AWS 命令行界面（CLI）和 AWS SDK 访问此功能。此功能已在支持 Amazon EBS 卷克隆的所有 AWS 区域推出，包括所有商业区域、AWS GovCloud（美国）区域、AWS 中国区域以及受支持的本地区域。 要了解更多信息，请参阅 Amazon EBS 卷克隆文档 。

items.title: 适用于 AD 的 AWS 私有 CA EKS 插件和连接器现已在 AWS GovCloud（美国）区域推出
items.summary: AWS 私有证书颁发机构（AWS 私有 CA）宣布，适用于 Kubernetes 的 AWS 私有 CA 连接器已作为托管的 Amazon EKS 插件和适用于 Active Directory 的 AWS 私有 CA 连接器，在 AWS GovCloud（美国东部）和 AWS GovCloud（美国西部）区域推出。此次发布扩展了 AWS GovCloud（美国）客户在管理政府工作负载时可用的证书自动化功能。 适用于 Kubernetes 的 AWS 私有 CA 连接器 EKS 插件通过 EKS 控制台、CLI 和 API，提供简化的安装、配置和生命周期管理。该连接器与证书管理器配合使用，自动执行证书请求、向 Kubernetes 分发密钥并续订，为入口控制器启用 TLS，并保护 Istio 和 Linkerd 等服务网格中的服务间通信。 借助适用于 Active Directory 的 AWS 私有 CA 连接器，AWS GovCloud（美国）客户可以将 AWS 私有 CA 作为其已加入 Active Directory 的对象的证书颁发机构。该连接器通过熟悉的 Microsoft 证书注册界面，为已加入域的用户、计算机和其他对象自动颁发证书，支持智能卡身份验证、LDAPS 和网络设备身份验证（802.1x）等企业场景。 AWS 私有 CA 使用 FIPS 140-3 第 3 级硬件安全模块（HSM）保护私钥材料。 要开始使用，请参阅 AWS 私有 CA 产品页面 、 Amazon EKS 插件用户指南 和 适用于 Active Directory 的 AWS 私有 CA 连接器文档 。

items.title: Amazon Connect Customer Profiles 现可在客户进入或退出细分群体时发送事件
items.summary: Amazon Connect Customer Profiles 现可发送细分群体成员资格事件，使您能够在客户档案进入或退出细分群体（例如高价值客户或低满意度客户）时，接收实时和预定通知。以前，检测客户档案何时加入或离开细分群体，需要定期导出整个细分群体，并运行自定义脚本来识别差异。这一手动流程不仅消耗资源，还会引入错误，并在客户符合某细分群体条件与下游系统采取行动之间造成数小时的延迟。 借助细分群体成员资格事件，Customer Profiles 会自动评估成员资格变更，并将其直接流式传输到您的 Amazon Kinesis 数据流。对于使用标准条件构建的细分群体，变更会在档案属性更新时近实时检测到。对于增强型细分群体（使用 Spark SQL），周期性快照会按可配置的间隔评估成员资格，并通知您相关变更。每个事件都包含档案 ID、细分群体名称、操作类型（已加入或已离开），以及检测到的变更是实时还是在计划运行期间发生的，为您提供在数秒（而非数小时）内激活出站营销活动、个性化工作流或留存行动所需的一切信息。 您可以在提供 Amazon Connect Customer Profiles 的所有 AWS 区域，开始使用细分群体成员资格事件。要开始使用，请在您的域设置中配置 Amazon Kinesis 数据流并订阅细分群体。有关更多信息，请参阅我们的 管理员指南 。有关 Amazon Connect Customer Profiles 的更多信息，请访问我们的 产品页面 。

items.title: 适用于 Amazon CloudFront 的动态图像转换新增四项功能
items.summary: 今天，AWS 宣布适用于 Amazon CloudFront 的动态图像转换（DIT）新增四项功能。DIT 是一种支持 AWS 的解决方案，可帮助客户根据其需求转换图像。 客户现在可以使用增强的智能裁剪功能，该功能具备自定义标签检测和高级构图控制，可在裁剪后的图像中保留产品、文本、徽标和自定义对象。此外，客户还可受益于增强的自动图像优化功能，该功能利用 CloudFront 的多层设备检测技术，为从手机、平板电脑到智能电视等各类浏览器和设备提供尺寸适配的图像，从而最大限度地扩大优化覆盖范围，而不受用户访问内容的方式的限制。DIT 还推出了一个交互式图像转换平台，用于测试和验证转换效果，并实现了其 ECS 和 Lambda 架构之间的完全功能对等。 DIT 增强的智能裁剪功能使客户能够将多种检测方法（包括人脸、标签、文本、徽标以及自定义的 Amazon Rekognition 模型）整合到单个请求中，并可根据业务需求优先级配置宽高比、内边距和重力约束。增强的自动优化功能现采用分层检测方法，在客户端提示后面叠加 CloudFront 的设备分类标头和可配置的回退策略，从而消除了此前导致约 30% 的流量无法得到优化的浏览器支持差距，并将适配尺寸的图像交付范围从浏览器扩展至所有设备类型。该图像转换平台会显示经过转换的图像，并提供扩展指标，包括原始和输出维度、格式、文件大小、压缩比以及处理时间，从而使客户能够验证其转换策略的性能。 DIT 已在所有商业区域以及以下四个需主动启用的区域推出：亚太地区（香港）、中东（巴林）、非洲（开普敦）、欧洲地区（米兰）。 要了解更多信息，请访问 DIT 解决方案页面 。

items.title: Amazon EMR 为迁移旧版本的客户扩展了支持，不收取额外费用
items.summary: Amazon EMR 现在让您有更多时间，在旧版本到达支持终止日期之前完成迁移，且无需支付额外费用。如果您正在积极迁移，则在符合条件的版本上运行的工作负载，在您迁移到当前版本期间将继续获得支持，无需主动启用，也不收取任何费用。 为了让您有更多时间进行规划和迁移，Amazon EMR 将尽可能针对 5.36 和 6.6 至 6.15 版本提供关键安全修复，直至 2027 年 6 月 30 日；并将针对 7.0 至 7.10 版本提供扩展标准支持，直至 2027 年 8 月 31 日。如需获得扩展支持，请联系 AWS Support，告知您的迁移计划以及升级所需的任何帮助。 该支持适用于 Amazon EMR 的所有部署模式（EMR on EC2、EMR on EKS 和 EMR Serverless），已在提供 Amazon EMR 的所有 AWS 区域推出。有关版本及其支持日期的完整列表，请参阅 Amazon EMR 标准支持政策 。如需获得扩展支持，请联系 AWS Support 并提供您的迁移计划，或使用 Apache Spark 升级代理 将您的应用程序迁移到最新版本。
